summary: The three mini games play well now: clear start cards, a HUD that says where to go, end cards with a level, a best and somewhere your catch goes, and I won or finished each on a first try. Live motion is much better (8 of 10 creatures clean in a busy afternoon, 10 of 10 at noon). But everything new since s104 is to watch, not to play. The newest ideas (the TV, the word round, the drift wake) still use placeholder looks, and a player who has once used the free camera gets a jump-in where Lumi is a speck over the sea.

lighting.why: Unchanged: one sun on clay, the same noon look in eye-level 0112 as in earlier day shots; the TV screen is unlit-bright live but lights nothing. Dusk lamps (s107) are the only real light. The traced dusk sawtooth (#498) is still open.

materials.why: Traced TV (reviews/p112/tv-traced.png): matte brown cuboids, a flat black knob panel, a picture with no glass, coat or reflection. The pond has a medium since s110; the rest is one clay/plastic look. The drift wake is flat white discs.

world.why: Progress shots 0109 vs 0112 show the same island; the palm islets make the drift film's sea alive. Up close the face hill is a blurry stretched texture that fills a third of the follow view (cam-follow-3.png) and reads as a yellow slug with stripes, not Lumi's face (jis.jpg).

props.why: Good generated assets everywhere (cottage, easels, pumpkins, swing, palm islets), but the newest prop, the TV, is a box built from cuboids (tv-raster.png) while its generated mesh lies unused.

creatures.why: Same cast with hats and the chick that follows Lumi. Hide and seek's 'hiders' stand in the open (hss.jpg: the pig 'hiding' on bare grass). The word round lives only in speech text.

animation.why: Up from 5: my own measure at 11:40 gave 10 of 10 moving well, and at 14:00 (snow day, TV watchers, fishing) 8 of 10 twice, against 1 of 10 at s109. What is left: Hopscotch judders (96% of frames), jumps 0.34 m in a frame and moves at 10 m/s while its goal is :sleep, and its yellow cap shows in 6 frames and is gone in the next 2 (motion-c/motion.png). The films are smooth apart from the TV film's camera.

fun.why: Firefly catch (7/8, the catch goes to the lantern), hide and seek (4/4 in 36 s, level 2 next) and the berry race (won 9-5, level 2 next) each have a goal, feedback and a reason to replay. But the berry rivals scored all 5 berries in the first 18 s and none in the 35 s after, and nothing new has been playable since s104.

wow.why: The TV Droste tunnel is a shareable idea, spoiled by the camera pushing through the pig's head and stray bubbles at the key moment. The word round is a lovely concept that is invisible in 3D. The drift with palm islets is the prettiest of the three films.

camera.why: Follow mode: views past posts and the face hill's smear, with Lumi cut at the frame's edge (cam-follow-1..3). Jump-in after the free camera has been used: a far orbit with Lumi a speck over the sea, and switching to follow does not bring the chase view back (jfs.jpg). With follow chosen first, the chase view is good (jcs.jpg). TV film: the push-in goes through creatures. Orbit is a fine wide view.

ui.why: Mini game cards and HUDs are clear and readable. The jump-in key strip lists 16 keys, but from the camera half of them (C sing, B bubble) show nothing a player can see. 'New on the island' and the message are true.

style.why: One clay look, broken by the cuboid TV, the stretched hill texture and the white foam coins.

performance.why: Sandbox frame median 2.6 ms, p95 5.4 ms (before it froze); the human's game 2.7/5.7 ms per the journal; TV and word round 0.0 ms.

findings.title: Something new to PLAY after six watch-only sessions
findings.what: I played all three mini games and they are good, but they are the same three as at s104. Drafts, the word round, the TV, the drift and the moody camera are all things to watch. Goals 1 and 3 have stalled.
findings.evidence: reviews/p112/ffs.jpg, hss.jpg, brs.jpg (the only games in the menu); progress dashboard 0109 vs 0112
findings.suggestion: Make one of the recent ideas playable: 'telephone' (carry a word to a friend before it is misheard), a TV remote that switches the island's weather or era, or steering the drifting island to an islet. Goal 3's physics (Maelstrom water, paint, pumpkins) is the other open road.
findings.done_when: A fourth item under Mini game with a start card, goal, score, end card with R to play again, and a passing first-play W/A/D test

findings.title: Real television: the generated TV set with glass, wood coat and brass
findings.what: The TV on the meadow is brown cuboids with a flat quad screen. When traced it is matte everywhere, with no glass on the screen and no gloss on the wood. The generated TV mesh is finished and unused.
findings.evidence: reviews/p112/tvs.jpg (raster and traced, same view from 5 m)
findings.suggestion: Swap in the mesh (shadow plate cut, facing checked), the picture quad under a thin Glass or coated layer that reflects the sky when traced, clearcoat wood, Conductor brass knobs, and in traced copies a soft screen glow that lights the watchers' faces.
findings.done_when: A traced still from the same eye: a sky reflection on the screen, a highlight on the wood, the TV's silhouette no longer a box

findings.title: TV film camera: no pushing through heads and bubbles on the way in
findings.what: In 'The island on TV' the dolly passes through the pig's head, then a crab's claws and a cloud of pale bubbles cover the lower half and the screen, right at the moment the tunnel should take over the frame.
findings.where: movies/tv.jl camera path; bubbles in quiet copies
findings.suggestion: Route the push over or between the watchers, keep other events out of the take, and end on the screen filling the frame, pushing into the 3rd and 4th nested TV.
findings.done_when: A new take where no creature fills more than 10% of any frame after 5 s, no bubbles, and the last frame is at least 70% screen

findings.title: Jump-in always gets the chase view, even after the free camera was used
findings.what: After I had picked 'Camera: free' once, Play (jump in) gave a far orbit around Lumi: Lumi a speck flying over the sea, later hidden behind crowns. Picking follow during the jump-in did not bring the chase view back. Every key I pressed (X, G, P, B, V, H) was invisible from there. Picking follow BEFORE Play gives a good chase view.
findings.evidence: reviews/p112/jis.jpg and jfs.jpg (free kept) vs jcs.jpg (follow first)
findings.suggestion: A jump-in starts in the chase view every time; the free camera is something the player turns on during it (drag), and the camera menu works during play. Make every key's effect big enough to read from the chase view (C: notes that rise, B: a bubble round Lumi).
findings.done_when: Pick free, then Play: the first screenshot shows Lumi from behind at least 1/5 of the frame high; after X, C and B each a screenshot shows the effect

findings.title: Berry race rivals keep racing for the whole minute
findings.what: In my race the three critters scored 2, 2 and 1 in the first 18 s and nothing in the 35 s after (scores [2,2,1] at 18, 34 and 50 s), so the second half was me picking berries alone and the 9-5 win was never in doubt.
findings.evidence: state samples while playing: (:playing, 4, [2,2,1], 18 s), (5, [2,2,1], 34 s), (8, [2,2,1], 50 s); reviews/p112/brs.jpg
findings.suggestion: Log why each rival stops (no berry left near it, a goal taken by another plugin such as the snow day or TV watching), and keep them in the race (RACE_GOALS) until the end. A close race decided in the last seconds is the fun.
findings.done_when: Three races: every rival scores at least once after the 30 s mark in each

findings.title: Hopscotch: no judder, 10 m/s slides or cap that blinks
findings.what: In the 14:00 afternoon the rest move well, but Hopscotch (goal :sleep) moves at 10 m/s, jumps 0.34 m in a frame, its body judders in 96% of frames, and its yellow cap is there in 6 consecutive frames and gone in the next 2.
findings.where: the crab body (makeover.jl crab), outfits.jl, whatever moves a 'sleeping' crab
findings.evidence: reviews/p112/motion-b and motion-c (sense_motion! at 14:00, 8 of 10 moving well twice); motion-c/motion.png frames 7-8
findings.suggestion: Find who moves a sleeping crab (a plugin setting pos every frame?) and keep outfits on the herd's drawn frame.
findings.done_when: Two measures at 14:00: 9 of 10 or better, no creature faster than 4 m/s, and no outfit missing in a steps sheet

findings.title: The face hill: a crisp texture up close and a face from the overview
findings.what: In follow views the face hill is a blurry, stretched yellow smear taking a third of the frame. From jump-in heights it reads as a yellow slug with black stripes, not Lumi's face.
findings.suggestion: Paint it in vertex colours or a sharper texture with the eyes and beak as shapes (raised beak, sunken eyes), and keep the follow camera from parking against its side.
findings.done_when: A follow screenshot near it with no smeared texels, and the overview where someone who doesn't know would say 'a bird's face'

findings.title: The drift's wake: one streaming foam V from the stern, not white coins
findings.what: In 'Past the palm islands' the wake is scattered flat white ellipses, the one placeholder left in the best shot of the session.
findings.suggestion: A ribbon of foam along the two stern lines with a noisy texture fading with age, plus bow spray.
findings.done_when: A drift frame where the wake reads as two continuous foam lines, no separate discs

engine.what: Calling NeverendingGame.live(...) inside a live eval (here live("motion")) connects the game to its own socket and blocks on readline while the frame loop that would answer is the one waiting: the sandbox froze for good during this review and does not answer status. live() should refuse when called inside the game it addresses, or an eval should time out. The host must restart the sandbox.
engine.evidence: dev/NeverendingGame/src/live.jl:181-197 and handle_live_commands!; tools/live.py status times out since 08:44

engine.what: Hikari SunSkyLight leaves the sky black below the horizon, the sawtooth in traced dusk pictures (#498).

process: After freezing the sandbox I ran a private copy of it (the same plugins and world, a scratch state root under reviews/p112/root) and did the checks there: every camera mode, all four menu entries played for about a minute, a traced still, and the motion measure at noon and 14:00. The author's ideas stay bold and unguessable (goal 8), and the film and post each session serve goals 2 and 5. Live motion has really improved (goal 6, 1/10 -> 8/10 in the busy afternoon). The pattern that holds the scores down is finish: each idea ships at about 70% and the next session moves on. The TV mesh lies unused, the wake is still coins after two reviews, the word is invisible, and the face hill does not read. Goal 1 (playable interactions) and goal 3 (physics, Mantle/Maelstrom) have had nothing new for six sessions, and goal 7 got only the pond's medium. Next session: the real TV with traced materials and a clean push-in take, the jump-in camera, and a playable version of one recent idea before any new concept.
